messages:
olivia: quick question — i've been prototyping a 'seed-only' bootstrap image + delta manifest approach for airgapped installs. tradeoff is smaller seed but more complex partial sync logic. thoughts? :thinking:

mateo: curious — what's in the seed exactly? root CA, runtime, minimal model manifest?

olivia: minimal runtime, verifier binary, CA bundle, and a tiny index (~5MB) that lists top-level artifact shards. no models. idea is customers bring the seed on usb, then operator can bring deltas later via rsync/usb.

rachel: sounds safer for initial install. main risk i see is rollout correctness when partial deltas fail — how do we ensure atomic activation?

olivia: two pieces: 1) manifest-level activation marker (signed) that references content-addressed layers, 2) apply agent that stages into ephemeral dir and performs integrity checks before swap. if any check fails, agent rolls back staging and reports.

jamal: how does rollback work if the old content was GC'd on disk to save space? we can't assume infinite retention on devices.

olivia: good point — plan is a small retention window + tombstone metadata in manifest. we keep last N activation entries in a lightweight journal. if old layers are GC'd we fallback to fallback-image pinned in seed (a conservative known-good bundle).

mateo: that fallback-image increases seed size though. any heuristics on what to include vs rely on deltas?

olivia: propose include a single fallback bundle limited to control-plane only (~50–100MB) to avoid full model carriage. it's primarily operator-facing.

rachel: what about verifier trust? need to avoid TOCTOU between verifying manifest and fetching shards. consider double-signed manifest or a signed manifest + per-shard sigs.

olivia: currently using manifest.sig (root signing key) + each shard has a sha256 in the manifest. fetcher verifies shard checksum after download, then the agent re-checks the manifest binding before activation. code sketch:

```
# fetch
curl -sfS $SHARD_URL -o /tmp/shard
sha256sum -c <<EOF
$EXPECTED_HASH  /tmp/shard
EOF
# verify manifest binding
verify-manifest --manifest /var/lib/seed/manifest.json --signer /etc/seed/root.pem
```

jamal: ok. one operational concern: customers often have flaky usb transfer or limited bandwidth. we should support resume + partial-de-dup across bundles. content-addressed blobs help. also add a small progress/verify mode in UI.

olivia: agreed. i want to propose a hybrid: content-addressed storage with a compact chunk index in seed that lets fetcher request only missing chunk ranges. then deltas can be packaged as chunk manifests referencing same blobs.

mateo: sounds good. two follow-ups: 1) safety net for activation (circuit breaker + healthcheck window), 2) operator tooling for manual restore if journal gets corrupted.

rachel: also add a clear operator playbook for airgapped restores — small runbook that says: verify seed signature -> attach delta media -> run staged-apply -> wait for healthchecks -> confirm. that helps support.

olivia: i'll draft an RFC that includes: seed layout, journal format, manifest + per-shard sig strategy, GC policy (retain last 3 activations), and chunked partial-sync protocol. will post next week.

deploy-bot: deployment job #deploy/airgap-proto started by olivia — logs at https://ci.internal/jobs/4521 :shipit:

jamal: nice. one last nit — metrics: record activation_attempt, activation_success, verification_failures, fallback_used. makes it easier to tune GC window.

olivia: noted. adding metrics + runbook to RFC. thanks all! :raised_hands:
